speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the findings of the Auditor-General’s Report for FY 2021/22 (a) what remedial actions are being taken by SkillsFuture Singapore in light of frauds and lapses in the disbursement of grants; (b) how much has been defrauded or overpaid since the inception of SkillsFuture; (c) how much have been recovered; and (d) whether any individuals overseeing the grant schemes have been or will be held accountable for the loss of public funds.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Education regarding the FY 2021/22 Auditor-General's Report finding that SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) was lax in collecting Skills Development Levy (SDL) funds (a) what are the reasons and root causes as to why the discrepancy is not detected over five years; (b) how long will it take for SSG to collect back the required funds; and (c) what does the agency intend to do to prevent such similar grant management issues from occurring in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, may I have your permission to combine the response to Question Nos 1 and 2 by Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Yip Hon Weng?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The Auditor-General’s Office (AGO) had identified lapses in two areas in the audit of SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG): overpayment in grant disbursement and under-collection of Skills Development Levy.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The main causes of these lapses were due to inaccurate or erroneous declarations by grant applicants and training providers that were not picked up by SSG’s internal checks.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The bulk of such errors occurred prior to November 2020, when SSG’s previous IT system for grant administration had used a declaration-based approach.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Other errors also occurred during manual processing of grants, including human errors made by the service provider contracted by SSG to perform grant administration functions.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG has contacted all affected training providers, companies and individuals for the necessary recovery.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Parties will be given time to check their own records and return any confirmed overpayment.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: To reduce reliance on declarations and manual processing, SSG implemented a new IT system for administering Training Grants since November 2020.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The system uses administrative data in Government databases to determine and verify eligibility of the grant applicants.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG is also streamlining its business rules to rely less on declared information and manual verification.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Where these cannot be avoided, SSG will tighten its audits on payments disbursed and on the work of its service provider.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Allow me to explain the SDL and how it is collected today.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The SDL is a levy which companies pay every month for both their local and foreign employees in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The SDL payable for each employee is 0.25% of the monthly total wages.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG derives estimates of SDL payable by companies based on existing Government data such as CPF.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG’s estimates may differ from actual SDL amounts paid by the employers due to factors such as fluctuations in total wages paid to foreign workers every month, some of whom might be on home leave and not receiving salary during the period of home leave.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In some cases, the variance may be due to employers using more updated employee data, instead of being an actual under-payment of SDL.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG has adopted a risk-based approach to follow up on estimated variances.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This was achieved through IT system improvements and SSG’s reminder letters and calls.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Nevertheless, SSG acknowledges that more needs to be done to actively reconcile the remaining gap and help all employers pay the correct amount of SDL.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG will send timely payment reminders and develop more efficient processes to resolve differences in the companies' and SSG’s estimates of SDL payable.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For the few recalcitrant employers who do not pay the outstanding levies despite reminders, SSG will take decisive punitive actions.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Learning from the AGO audit, SSG will do even more to review and enhance its processes, policies and systems to prevent lapses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, whether errant vendors will be closely monitored to prevent similar situations from happening in the future?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Two, will SSG consider working with specialist agencies like GovTech to make sure that the computer system is up-to-date and to ensure that similar situations do not happen in the future?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Indeed, SSG will work more closely with GovTech and is actually looking at rolling out a new IT system to be able to estimate more accurately and be able to track the employers in the payment of SDL.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: By the middle of next year, we are hoping to roll out a new system to help employers as well, to estimate much better what is the SDL that they are liable for and also for SSG to be able to verify.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have four supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first is, AGO cited that there were $4.22 million of overpayment.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I would like clarification as to whether this is based on a 100% check by AGO or this is just what was found based on test checks, meaning there could be others that have not been detected so far.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, that is the first question: whether $4.22 million is based on a test check or a 100% check.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question: one of the lapses found was that there were payments made for courses that were actually not approved by SSG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The remedial action cited in the report was that retrospective approval would be obtained for these courses to be approved.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My question is: is this the correct approach to take?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Meaning that funding was paid out for unapproved courses, but now retrospective approval is being sought to approve those courses retrospectively.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The third question: whether the Ministry is considering taking any action against the outsourced service provider?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The fourth question: earlier, the Minister of State mentioned that if there was negligence found in these lapses, then actions will be taken.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: AGO actually mentioned that the business rules of SSG were not well-defined.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, the question is: how far up should this accountability go?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: First of all, I would like to say that the SDL Act has been around since 1979.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Prior to SSG, the Government was already collecting the Skills Development Levy.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Indeed, as AGO has pointed out, business rules have a certain looseness that needs to be tightened so that companies can better assess – more accurately as well – the SDL that is payable.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG is in the process of reviewing this.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In fact, we are also in the process of reviewing the SDL Act.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: With the review of upstream business rules, it will make it easier for companies to be able to estimate the SDL that is payable and for SSG to be able to collect more promptly the amount that companies owe to the Government.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about whether AGO had conducted 100% checks when they detected the $4.22 million of grant overpayment.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And amongst the transactions that they had checked, they found overpayments.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Just as an example, AGO found that through their own AGO database, there was overclaim of absentee payroll by employers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: What AGO did was, they looked at the salaries paid by companies over a 12-month period and they divided it by 12 to estimate the monthly salaries paid by the companies.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: But actually, it is more accurate for us, for SSG, to take a look at the salary that the company had paid to its employees in the month that the course was conducted.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, what I am trying to say is that, it is quite a complicated process and for the amounts that are estimated to be over payment of the grant, SSG is now in the process of doing verification and using more detailed data with the entities involved.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: To that question about whether retrospective approvals will be made, I think, what is more important is for us to understand the spirit of SkillsFuture courses.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SkillsFuture courses are meant to help individuals as well as employers with upskilling.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think what matters to us most at the end of the day is, whether the individuals and companies are eligible for the grants that they have applied for.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: If the lapses in application were due to administrative errors, then we would want to look at how we can help these individuals, companies and the training providers in rectifying this in a proper way.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: At the moment, I think the root cause that we have identified is the massive volume of manual processing.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It makes it very, very difficult for all the verifications to be done fully.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And hence, there needs to be more upstream changes in policies and business rules.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I do not know whether part (b) and (c) of my filed Parliamentary Questions were answered.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, is the Minister of State able to tell us how much has been defrauded or overpaid since inception and how much has been recovered?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am sorry if I missed your answer, but I do not recall hearing that the answer to (b) and (c).

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have not used that term yet, because, as I explained, there is a lengthy verification process with the individuals and the companies and training providers involved.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Since SSG was formed, there have been fraud cases detected.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As to how much is being recovered, SSG is still in the process of following up with individuals and the companies and they will need some time.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is not very easy to do the verification quickly.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, we ask the Members to allow SSG some time to recover the overpayments.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Patrick Tay, last supplementary question, on this topic, please.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I just want to make an appeal and ask MOE, especially SkillsFuture Singapore, to not because of this episode, hold back SkillsFuture funding for employers, workers, Singaporeans, who actually genuinely want to undergo lifelong learning and Continuing Education and Training (CET).

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Therefore, I really hope this does not hold back the generous funding and support for lifelong learning and CET.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is our collective desire to make sure that Singaporeans have access to sufficient SkillsFuture opportunities and resources.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: At the same time, we need to make sure that the money is being accounted for properly and being used wisely.
